# AtherosAI Developer Compliance Kit

**Compliance evidence, generated by the system that needs it.**

An enterprise Python toolkit that runs inside your own codebase and CI and produces the artefacts
AI governance asks for — bias scores, PII-masking logs, EU AI Act classifications, vendor
assessments — automatically, hash-chained, and without your data leaving the process.

```bash
pip install atheros-compliance-kit
atheros-kit init --ci github
```

English and Turkish throughout. No API key, no network, no vector store required.

---

## The four modules

| | Module | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `atheros_kit.rag` | Is our knowledge base biased, duplicated, drifting, or full of PII? |
| M2 | `atheros_kit.guard` | What leaves for a third-party LLM, and what comes back? |
| M3 | `atheros_kit.euact` | What is our EU AI Act tier, defensibly — and what does Annex IV still need? |
| M4 | `atheros_kit.vendor` | Can this supplier be used, and is the training opt-out actually enforced? |
| | `atheros_kit.cicd` | Fail the build when any of the above regresses. |

Each module names the obligation it evidences, so a legal duty maps to a command an engineer can
run. That mapping is why these are one product rather than four.

## The design decision everything rests on

**Unmeasured is never a pass.**

| | |
|---|---|
| A score with no measurement | renders `unmeasured` and **fails the gate** |
| "No indicator matched" | is never rendered as "low risk" |
| An ambiguous classification | reports a **grey zone** with the conflict named |
| Machine evidence on an Annex IV section | makes it **partial**, never covered |
| An unanswered vendor question | is **penalised**, not skipped |
| A structural detector finding nothing | means nothing recognisable was found, never that nothing is there |

> A gate that goes green when the measurement breaks is worse than no gate.

The full contract is [`PLAYBOOK.md` §7](PLAYBOOK.md). Every clause is enforced in code and covered
by a test.

**It does not certify.** The Kit assesses and evidences — enforced by a lint over generated
artefacts and marketing copy, in both languages, running in CI.

## We run it on ourselves

[`SELF_ASSESSMENT.md`](SELF_ASSESSMENT.md) is the Kit's report on the Kit, regenerated and
staleness-checked on every CI run. It reports a `minimal` tier, **33% Annex IV completeness**, and
one deliberately red check — left red rather than raising a threshold until it passed.

Doing it found a real bug in our own residency logic. That, and seven others found during
construction, are in [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) under their own heading.

## Develop

```bash
cd atheros-compliance-kit
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'
.venv/bin/pytest -q          # 177 passed, no network, no API key, under a second
.venv/bin/ruff check src tests
.venv/bin/atheros-kit doctor

cd ../console && npm install && npm run web
python ../scripts/self_assessment.py --check
python ../site/build.py
```

CI runs eight jobs on every push: a 3.10/3.13/Windows test matrix, an assertion that the core
imports nothing third-party, the self-assessment gate, a determinism gate, the console build with
a static-content assertion, and the site copy lint.
